questions.question: Which design goal specifies that all traffic from inside to outside, and vice versa, must traverse the firewall?
options: Mandatory Transit
Policy Enforcement
Self-Immunity
Deep Packet Inspection
questions.answer: Mandatory Transit

questions.question: A packet filtering firewall makes forwarding decisions primarily based on which criteria?
options: The application-level payload content
The state of the active TCP connection
Fields in the IP and transport-level headers
Behavioral patterns of the network traffic
questions.answer: Fields in the IP and transport-level headers

questions.question: What is a primary disadvantage of using an application-level gateway compared to a packet filter?
options: It cannot inspect the contents of the payload
It introduces significant processing overhead
It is highly vulnerable to IP spoofing attacks
It allows direct connections between internal and external hosts
questions.answer: It introduces significant processing overhead

questions.question: How does a stateful inspection firewall improve upon a simple packet filter for client-server applications?
options: It encrypts all outbound traffic automatically
It tracks the state of active TCP connections to allow return traffic
It uses a proxy to relay application commands
It operates exclusively at the physical layer
questions.answer: It tracks the state of active TCP connections to allow return traffic

questions.question: A circuit-level gateway is most commonly used for which of the following scenarios?
options: Filtering spam from incoming email traffic
Inspecting HTTP GET requests for SQL injection
Relaying outbound connections from trusted internal users
Blocking all ICMP traffic at the network edge
questions.answer: Relaying outbound connections from trusted internal users

questions.question: Which firewall basing option involves a software module on a server intended to provide tailored protection regardless of network topology?
options: Personal Firewall
Host-Based Firewall
Network Device Firewall
Bastion Host
questions.answer: Host-Based Firewall

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a DMZ (Demilitarized Zone) in a firewall topology?
options: To provide a secure tunnel for remote workers
To host internal-only databases away from the perimeter
To isolate external-facing servers from the internal network
To bypass the firewall for high-speed streaming data
questions.answer: To isolate external-facing servers from the internal network

questions.question: In a DMZ configuration with two firewalls, what is typically the role of the internal firewall?
options: To provide the first line of defense against Internet scans
To protect the internal network from both external threats and DMZ systems
To act as the primary VPN termination point for all users
To filter outbound traffic from the internal network to the DMZ only
questions.answer: To protect the internal network from both external threats and DMZ systems

questions.question: Why are firewalls considered a logical place to terminate a Virtual Private Network (VPN)?
options: The firewall is the only device capable of AES encryption
VPN traffic does not require inspection if it is encrypted
Termination behind the firewall prevents inspection of the decrypted traffic
VPNs are required by law to terminate at the network edge
questions.answer: Termination behind the firewall prevents inspection of the decrypted traffic

questions.question: Which security technology integrates multiple functions like firewalling, IPS, and antivirus into a single appliance?
options: HIPS
Snort Inline
Unified Threat Management (UTM)
Distributed Firewall
questions.answer: Unified Threat Management (UTM)

questions.question: What is a major performance consideration when deploying a Unified Threat Management (UTM) appliance?
options: It can only handle one security protocol at a time
It requires a separate license for every internal user
It can suffer from throughput losses of 50% or more
It cannot be used in networks that utilize VLANs
questions.answer: It can suffer from throughput losses of 50% or more

questions.question: A Network-Based IPS (NIPS) differs from a standard NIDS primarily because it:
options: Is located on the endpoint rather than the network
Only monitors encrypted traffic flows
Operates inline and can discard malicious packets
Uses fewer system resources than a passive IDS
questions.answer: Operates inline and can discard malicious packets

questions.question: Which Snort Inline rule type is used to drop a packet and log the event?
options: Reject
Drop
Sdrop
Replace
questions.answer: Drop

questions.question: The 'Replace' option in Snort Inline is particularly useful for which application?
options: Replacing expired SSL certificates on the fly
Changing the source IP of every outgoing packet
Disabling attacks in honeypot deployments
Upgrading the protocol version of old applications
questions.answer: Disabling attacks in honeypot deployments

questions.question: Which mechanism is often used by Host-Based IPS (HIPS) to protect against malicious mobile code?
options: Sandboxing
Port knocking
Deep packet inspection
Circuit-level relaying
questions.answer: Sandboxing

questions.question: An administrator wants to prevent internal users from accessing unauthorized external websites while ensuring minimal latency for approved connections. Which firewall type is most efficient for this outbound relay?
options: Application-level gateway
Circuit-level gateway
Stateless packet filter
Personal firewall
questions.answer: Circuit-level gateway

questions.question: You are designing a network for a small company that needs web protection, email filtering, and a VPN, but has limited IT staff. Which solution is most appropriate?
options: A distributed firewall with separate sensors
A cluster of high-performance bastion hosts
A Unified Threat Management (UTM) appliance
Individual host-based firewalls on every machine
questions.answer: A Unified Threat Management (UTM) appliance

questions.question: An organization detects a sophisticated attack that bypasses the perimeter firewall by using encrypted HTTPS traffic. Which additional layer would be most effective at blocking the attack at the target server?
options: An external packet filter
A Host-Based IPS (HIPS)
A stateless router
A bastion host in the DMZ
questions.answer: A Host-Based IPS (HIPS)

questions.question: To prevent an attacker from using 'tiny fragment' attacks to bypass security rules, which action should a packet filtering firewall take?
options: Allow all fragments to ensure data integrity
Discard fragments that do not contain the minimum header information
Reassemble the entire file before checking the header
Convert the fragments into a single application-level proxy request
questions.answer: Discard fragments that do not contain the minimum header information

questions.question: Which policy approach is generally considered more secure for a firewall configuration?
options: Default Forward (allow all unless explicitly denied)
Default Discard (deny all unless explicitly allowed)
Open Perimeter (trust all internal traffic)
Hybrid Trust (allow all known MAC addresses)
questions.answer: Default Discard (deny all unless explicitly allowed)
